name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 216 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 25% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 216 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 25 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Manipur remains volatile as the state high court has kept the census on hold until April 2027 while the government reports over 4,000 firearms recovered and the transfer of the Kuki youths murder case to the NIA, with the chief minister meeting the victims' families and the home minister pledging safe return of displaced persons. In Kashmir, a six-year-old boy was killed by a leopard in Baramulla and a 27-year-old man died when an unidentified vehicle struck his scooter in Srinagar. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Manipur forblir ustabil ettersom delstats høyesterett har holdt folketellingen på vent frem til april 2027, mens regjeringen rapporterer at over 4 000 skytevåpen er blitt funnet og at drapssaken mot Kuki-ungdom overføres til NIA, med statsministeren som møter ofrenes familier og innenriksministeren som lover trygg tilbakeføring av fordrevne. I Kashmir ble en six år gammel gutt drept av en leopard i Baramulla, og en 27 år gammel mann døde da et ukjent kjøretøy traff scooteren hans i Srinagar. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
